Moral

MOR-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Moral is concerned with what is right and wrong behavior; honest and good.

Returning the lost wallet was the moral thing to do.

Worked Example

Aesop's fables always end with a moral lesson, like 'slow and steady wins the race.'

The fable teaches what is right and what is wrong. Lessons about right and wrong are moral lessons.

How Moral Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

honest

honest: truthful and fair

good

good: kind and right

Antonyms

dishonest

dishonest: lying or cheating

unfair

unfair: not treating people right

How Strong Is It? — Nice → Heroic → moral

Nice vs. moral

Nice vs. moral: Nice is milder: sharing your crayons is nice, but it is not a big question of right and wrong.

Heroic vs. moral

Heroic vs. moral: Heroic is stronger: pulling a friend away from a speeding car is heroic, far beyond an everyday good deed.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mor

root — mor: custom, habit (Latin (mos, moris))

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Mor- means customs and habits, so moral describes the good habits of doing what is right.

Use the root in a new word: morale

Use the root in a new word: morale: After winning the relay, the team's morale was sky-high.

Root Check

Word Choice

Use moral when you talk about right and wrong, like a moral choice or a moral lesson in a story. As a noun, 'the moral' means the lesson itself.
